definitions.explanation: A proposal or tip presented as an easy way to make money. Usually carries a note of suspicion — the word most often appears in warnings about scams.

examples.japanese: ⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧{儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦しよう→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Be careful of too-good-to-be-true money-making schemes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}ちかけられた→持ちかける：06795_mochikakeru⟧。
examples.english: A friend approached me with a money-making proposition.

examples.japanese: ⟦{必|かなら}ず→必ず：01249_kanarazu⟧{儲|もう}かる⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{信|しん}じて→信じる：01111_shinjiru⟧⟦{投資|とうし}→投資：04711_toushi⟧し、⟦{結局|けっきょく}→結局：03815_kekkyoku⟧⟦{大金|たいきん}→大金：12192_taikin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{失|うしな}った→失う：01887_ushinau⟧。
examples.english: He believed a scheme that promised guaranteed profits, invested, and in the end lost a large sum.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{儲|もう}ける→儲ける：20583_moukeru⟧ (to make a profit) + ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧ (story, proposal), with the sequential voicing that turns はなし into ばなし in compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧{儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}: a too-good-to-be-true scheme
- {儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}ちかける→持ちかける：06795_mochikakeru⟧: to approach someone with a scheme
- {儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to go along with a scheme
- {儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}びつく: to jump at a money-making offer

USAGE:
The phrase ⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧{儲|もう}け{話|ばなし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ ("there is no easy money") is a set warning, and police and banks use {儲|もう}け{話|ばなし} in fraud-prevention campaigns. Treating one as genuine usually needs an explicit qualifier such as ⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧.
